claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The starting alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
Selective grain-boundary segregation of Al, Ti, and Cr accelerates degradation during high-temperature gas exposure.
Segregated Al, Ti, and Cr promote the formation of contiguous oxide channels.
Contiguous oxide channels compromise the protective behavior of the surface.
The bulk FCC matrix remains intact while oxide-channel-mediated degradation occurs.
Controlled post-processing annealing can minimize reactive-element segregation at grain boundaries.
The proposed annealing can reduce segregation without altering the FCC matrix structure.
Elevated temperature enhances grain-boundary diffusion in this alloy.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion causes preferential accumulation of reactive elements at grain boundaries.
Under oxidizing conditions, grain-boundary-segregated reactive elements form contiguous oxide channels.
Under reducing conditions, reactive-element segregation alters oxide-formation kinetics.
Minimizing reactive-element segregation retards oxidation.
Annealed samples with reduced grain-boundary segregation will have lower oxidation rates than as-built samples.
Annealed samples with reduced grain-boundary segregation will show a smaller mass change during exposure than as-built samples.
Annealed samples with reduced grain-boundary segregation will exhibit less intergranular oxide penetration than as-built samples.
The annealed samples will fully retain the starting alloy's high strength.
The annealed samples will fully retain the starting alloy's fatigue performance.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply from 700 to 850 °C in both oxidizing and reducing gas environments.
Exposure outside the stated conditions or for excessively long times may activate additional degradation pathways.
